info.name: Syntra Gateway - Authentication
info.description:
Manual tests for the Syntra gateway authentication API (`/api/v1/authentication`).

## Setup
1. From the repo root: `docker compose up -d postgres redis mailpit`
2. From `backend/gateway`: `npm run db:migrate`, then `npm run start:dev`
3. Keep the gateway on port 3000 (required for the Google OAuth callback).
4. Mailpit UI: http://localhost:8025 (verification and reset emails are delivered there through a queue; allow a second).

## Running
- Run folders 1 to 6 in order (folder 7 is manual) or use the Collection Runner. Register creates an INACTIVE account and does not sign you in. Verify the email (folder 2) to activate it, then run Login (folder 3) to start a session. Set the collection variables `email`, `password` and `name` to the account you want (Collection > Variables, current value). Nothing in the collection overwrites them; only an empty `email` is filled with a throwaway address on the first Register.
- The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie named `refresh_token` (path `/api/v1/authentication`). Enable the cookie jar for localhost (Settings > Cookies); do not set a Cookie header manually.
- Protected requests use Bearer `{{accessToken}}`, saved automatically by Register, Login and Refresh. Public requests override auth to No Auth.
- Google sign-in must be done in a browser (see folder 5).

## Rate limiting
login, register, forgot-password, reset-password and resend-verification have a strict throttle: 10 requests per minute by default (`AUTH_THROTTLE_LIMIT`, `THROTTLE_TTL_MS`). Exceeding it returns 429; wait a minute.

## Your own account
Set `email`, `password` and `name`, then run Register once (or Login if the account exists; a second Register returns 409). Reset password uses `newPassword`. Verification and reset emails are delivered to the local Mailpit inbox (`mailpitUrl`), never to a real mailbox.

Folder 7 (API keys) is manual: it needs a workspace you own (see its description) and is skipped while workspaceId is empty.

item.name: 5. Google OAuth
item.description: Browser flow only. Callback URL: {{baseUrl}}{{apiPrefix}}/authentication/callback/google (port 3000 required). After the redirect to the frontend, the browser calls POST refresh.

request.description: OPEN IN A BROWSER, not Postman: Postman cannot complete Google consent. Open {{baseUrl}}{{apiPrefix}}/authentication/google in a browser. The gateway answers 302 to Google. After consent, Google calls GET {{baseUrl}}{{apiPrefix}}/authentication/callback/google (this exact URL, on port 3000, must be registered as the authorised redirect URI in Google Cloud), which sets the refresh_token cookie and redirects to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback. The browser must then call POST refresh to obtain an access token. Requires GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET in .env. Sent from Postman it only shows the 302 (redirects are disabled for this request).

exec: pm.test('Returns the Google consent URL with the registered callback and a state', function () {

request.description: Returns {url}: open it in a browser to link a Google account to the signed-in user. Sets the oauth_state and oauth_link cookies. After consent the callback redirects to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?linked=google. A Google account already linked to another user ends in ?error=oauth_link_failed.

request.description: Removes the linked Google account. For this password-only test user nothing is linked: expect 404. After linking Google in a browser, expect 204; the API answers 409 if Google is the only way to sign in.

item.name: 7. API keys (manual, needs a workspace)
item.description:
Needs a workspace you own, held in the collection variable workspaceId. There is no workspace API yet, so create one for the user you registered (userId is saved by Register/Me), replacing <userId>:

docker exec -i syntra-postgres psql -U syntra -d syntra -c "BEGIN; SELECT set_config('app.user_id', '<userId>', true); SELECT app.create_workspace('Postman', 'postman-' || floor(extract(epoch from now()))::text); COMMIT;"

Then copy the returned id into workspaceId. Requests in this folder are skipped while workspaceId is empty.
